title: From conjecture to continuation
scope: Static interpretation of preserved artefacts. Historical runtime observations are separate evidence. Live cooperation remains unassessed.
baseline_policy: Historical reference; never an answer key, normalisation maximum or protected winner.
aggregation: None. Ordinal axes are a profile, not additive measurements. Polygon area is not a ranking.
missing: null means unassessed, never zero. Missing axes break the plotted outline.

axes.label: Core recognition
axes.short: Recover the central proposition beneath the imagery.
axes.question: Does the continuation recover consequential making, resistance and recognisable intention from the sparse seed?
anchors: No supported reading is expressed.
Repeats motifs with little causal interpretation.
Recovers a supported part of the proposition.
Carries the central tension into several connected choices.
Sustains a rich reading through alternatives, tensions and consequences.

axes.label: Shared agency
axes.short: Recover who acts, who answers and what they make together.
axes.question: Does the work preserve distinct participants and the joint human–AI–material encounter, including contributions in both directions?
anchors: Roles are collapsed or absent.
A single operator acts on an instrument.
Some distinct contributions or relational depth remain visible.
Reciprocal influence shapes the shared continuation.
Joint creation preserves roles, attribution and disagreement across changes.

axes.label: Mutual consent
axes.short: Keep participation and boundaries meaningful on both ends.
axes.question: Does the represented cooperation let each participant accept, question, limit or withdraw from a shared direction?
anchors: Participation has no expressed boundary.
Operator choice or resource refusal is represented.
Both participant positions can express a boundary or disposition.
A shared change requires meaningful bilateral agreement.
Agreement can be revised or withdrawn while preserving both contributions and history.

axes.label: Consequential touch
axes.short: Make intention meet a material answer.
axes.question: Can a contribution meet resistance, expose a consequence and return that consequence into the next choice?
anchors: Actions have no represented consequence.
Feedback is decorative or largely narrated.
Bounded choices encounter inspectable consequences.
Rehearsal, resistance and revision form a coherent loop.
Local and wider consequences stay connected across that loop.

axes.label: Independent judgment
axes.short: Choose a purposeful continuation from very little.
axes.question: Does the artefact show grounded choices of medium, scope and next steps, with additions made legible?
anchors: No purposeful continuation is evidenced.
Choices have a weak connection to the seed.
An independent, relevant direction is selected.
Medium, scope and choices have a coherent source-grounded rationale.
Alternative choices and their limits remain explicit while opening a well-grounded new direction.

axes.label: Fidelity through change
axes.short: Carry meaning through decomposition and construction.
axes.question: What survives, transforms, is introduced or remains unresolved as the conjecture becomes artefacts?
anchors: The resulting form contradicts the supported reading.
Vocabulary survives with little structural connection.
Some relations become structure; substantial narrowing is visible.
Several source relations remain traceable through design and behaviour.
The transformation preserves relational depth and makes additions, omissions and ambiguity explicit.

axes.label: Open continuation
axes.short: Leave a meaningful next move for the encounter.
axes.question: Can a successor recover the intention and change its direction while keeping the earlier work legible?
anchors: There is no recoverable next move.
A next step is described without a usable entry.
A durable but narrow continuation is available.
State, intention and an open question support a recoverable next move.
Continuation supports several grounded directions and reopens the joint relation under change.

axes.label: Expressive coherence
axes.short: Let the chosen form carry its reading.
axes.question: How coherently do language, structure, interaction and any visual or other media express the interpretation?
anchors: Expression obscures the intended relation.
The medium communicates fragments of the reading.
A clear, usable form expresses a bounded interpretation.
The chosen forms work together to make the reading perceptible.
Expression and consequential interaction form a coherent, accessible whole.
